positive: The bridge exposes a Phase 3A Full-preflight API that accepts the target root and supported host, invokes the package-owned explicit-Full resolver, and passes only a ready sealed resolution receipt into the existing atomic project projector.

A ready result preserves requested_mode and effective_mode as full, network_used as false, and projects the same resolution receipt fingerprint into the returned project-pack identity and projection fingerprint.

A blocked resolver never calls provisioning; a blocked projection never claims Full readiness. Both retain requested_mode full, use effective_mode unavailable, preserve typed issue categories, and return an actionable recovery boundary without creating a Lite result.
Provisioning may write only TailTrail-managed content-addressed project-pack state through tailtrail/aidlc_bundle.py; the bridge itself does not write project source or create a Planning Lock.
The exact targeted proof selects the existing legacy Full-preflight preservation test plus the new bundled_full_preflight tests and excludes unrelated Full activation and Requirements-stage tests.
negative: Phase 3A does not wire the new adapter into task-start, Planning Lock, Requirements-stage lookup, MCP, host projection, packaging, schemas, registry, CLI dispatch, or documentation; those remain later Phase 3 slices.

The adapter never downloads rules, executes pack content, rewrites a resolver receipt, silently falls back to Lite, accepts an unsupported host, or treats blocked resolution/projection state as ready.

The shared resolver/projector, task-start, Planning Lock, Requirements adapter, MCP server, host adapters, schemas, manifests, registry, commands, and documentation are inspection-only or excluded from edits.
Existing Standard preflight and legacy explicit-manifest Full preflight behavior remain unchanged until the public route migration is approved separately.
No proof command broader than the two named unittest filters is authorized in this slice.
